member.name: P:KPIEntry.Product
member.summary:
CdoId: 8850; FieldId: 27056; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:KPIEntry.RecipeName
member.summary: CdoId: 8850; FieldId: 27047; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Recipe Name

member.name: P:KPIEntry.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 8850; FieldId: 27058; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:KPIEntry.ResourceType
member.summary: CdoId: 8850; FieldId: 27060; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Resource Type, a Resource categorization. Resources with the same Resource Type may share the same Resources Status Model.; OriginalType: ResourceType

member.name: P:KPIEntry.RouteStep
member.summary: CdoId: 8850; FieldId: 27066; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A step in an ERPRoute, which is the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. ERP Route Steps are usually defined at a more summarized level than InSite workflow steps.; OriginalType: RouteStep

member.name: P:KPIEntry.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 8850; FieldId: 27062; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

CdoId: 8975; FieldId: 28692; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). member.name: P:ActivityWorkflowNavigator.CurrentActivity
member.summary:
CdoId: 9015; FieldId: 29264; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

member.name: P:ActivityWorkflowNavigator.DefaultNextActivity

A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

member.name: P:ActivityWorkflowNavigator.DefaultPath
member.summary:
CdoId: 9015; FieldId: 29267; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Path defines an allowable (Standard) move from one Step to another within a Workflow. Each Step contains zero or more (outbound) Paths. Only one of the Paths is the default Path, all others are alternate paths. If a Step contains any Paths, one must be the default. The default Route for a Workflow is determined by traversing through the Steps, starting at the first Step (defined in the workflow), using the default Path for each.
Paths are referenced by name or by Id. Path names are unique within the context of their Step.; OriginalType: Path

member.name: P:CIOOutboundDefinition.CIOChannelAdapter
member.summary:
CdoId: 4726826; FieldId: 673186360; Workspace: 10; Flags: Exposed, ReadOnly; Annotations: Channel Adapters provide an abstraction between the source system and the CIO Messaging System to allow the source system to send messages to the CIO Messaging System and receive messages from the CIO Messaging System without requiring the source system to directly consume the CIO endpoints. Channel Adapters provide a layer of abstraction to the external application to 'adapt' the Message Channel for convenience. Examples of Channel Adapters can be as simple as providing shared directories for passing files back and forth or as complex as accessing a source application's API to invoke the functionality inside an application necessary to retrieve and send data.
Camstar provides a standard set of Channel Adapters (e.g. ByFileAdapter), however, custom adapters can also be created for specific purposes (reference the Camstar CIO SDK).
; OriginalType: CIOChannelAdapter

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetails.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 4751907; FieldId: 28532; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetails.Parent
member.summary: CdoId: 4751907; FieldId: 679483733; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Id of the CDO containing this CDO.; OriginalType: ResourceLayout

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetails.Resource
member.summary: CdoId: 4751907; FieldId: 679483729; Workspace: csi; Flags: Exposed, ReadOnly; Annotations: i) Sub-class of Resource. ii) No maintenance service. iii) Provides common fields to its sub-classes.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetails.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 4751907; FieldId: 28530; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:ResourceLayoutDetails.WorkCenter
member.summary:
CdoId: 4751907; FieldId: 28534; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.
; OriginalType: WorkCenter

member.summary:
CdoId: 4841485; FieldId: 702548041; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

member.name: P:isPreactorScheduledOrders.LineAssignmentTmp
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841485; FieldId: 702548288; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.summary:
CdoId: 4841485; FieldId: 702547101; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. member.name: P:isIdealCycleTimes.Product
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841496; FieldId: 702546119; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:isIdealCycleTimes.ProductFamily
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841496; FieldId: 702546115; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Each Product can belong to a Product Family. Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.
Product Families are a slightly different concept from object groups. Grouping (Product bases, Operations, Resources, etc.) is done for validation and reporting. Groups are more free form and the application has less concrete knowledge of Groups (than Product Families). Another differentiation is that one object can belong to multiple Groups, but a product can only belong to one Product Family. Finally, Groups can contain other (sub-) Groups. Product Families can only contain Products.; OriginalType: ProductFamily

member.name: P:isOEEThruputDetails.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841497; FieldId: 702546133; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:isOEEThruputDetails.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841497; FieldId: 702546139; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isOEEThruputDetails.Step
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841497; FieldId: 702546142; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: SpecStep

member.name: P:isRecipePlanDetails.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841623; FieldId: 702547467; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isRecipePlanDetails.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841623; FieldId: 702547469; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.summary:
CdoId: 4841645; FieldId: 702547840; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.

member.name: P:isCompletedWIPSummary.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841645; FieldId: 702548121; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isCompletedWIPSummary.Workflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841645; FieldId: 702547848; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:isCompletedWIPSummary.WorkflowStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841645; FieldId: 702547839; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

member.name: P:isOEERawDetails.isProductFamily
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841500; FieldId: 702547902; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Each Product can belong to a Product Family. Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.
Product Families are a slightly different concept from object groups. Grouping (Product bases, Operations, Resources, etc.) is done for validation and reporting. Groups are more free form and the application has less concrete knowledge of Groups (than Product Families). Another differentiation is that one object can belong to multiple Groups, but a product can only belong to one Product Family. Finally, Groups can contain other (sub-) Groups. Product Families can only contain Products.; OriginalType: ProductFamily

member.name: P:isOEERawDetails.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841500; FieldId: 702546157; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:isOEERawDetails.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841500; FieldId: 702546156; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isOEERawDetails.RouteStep
member.summary: CdoId: 4841500; FieldId: 702548214; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A step in an ERPRoute, which is the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. ERP Route Steps are usually defined at a more summarized level than InSite workflow steps.; OriginalType: RouteStep

member.name: P:isOEERawDetails.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841500; FieldId: 702546159; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:isOEERawDetails.StartParentContainer
member.summary: CdoId: 4841500; FieldId: 702548243; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).; OriginalType: Container

member.name: P:isOEERawDetails.Step
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841500; FieldId: 702546152; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: SpecStep

member.name: P:isOEERawDetails.Workflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841500; FieldId: 702546154; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:LotSampleData.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 8593; FieldId: 23607; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.

Menu Definitions consist of a collection of predefined commands. Through the use of Menu Definitions the needs of different groups of employees can be met in a factory. For example, employees in an operation might be responsible for moving containers and collecting container parametric data, while employees in another operation might be responsible for starting and grouping containers. In both cases, they should see a different menu and therefore they would have a different Menu Definition.; OriginalType: MenuDefinition

member.name: P:ServiceHistoryDetail.DisplayName
member.summary: CdoId: 2530; FieldId: 6727; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character. This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used. DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

member.name: P:StartHistoryDetail.Workstation
member.summary:
CdoId: 2590; FieldId: 25857; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. member.name: P:ModelingAuditTrailHeader.Employee
member.summary:
CdoId: 7373; FieldId: 11479; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:DefectHistory.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 6850; FieldId: 25335; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:ResourceThruputHistory.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 6860; FieldId: 6438; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current status of each Preventative Maintenance for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Log-type Status Categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:ResourceThruputHistory.Run
member.summary: CdoId: 6860; FieldId: 6432; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Current Setup number. This value is used to identify all of the work that is performed using a specific Setup. The value is set (incremented) as part of the Resource Setup transaction. All Throughput and Movement transactions record this value in their history transactions.

member.name: P:ResourceThruputHistory.Setup
member.summary:
CdoId: 6860; FieldId: 6437; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Setup Definition describes the work required, materials required, and estimates how long it will take to setup for a specific task. A typical use of a Setup Definition is to describe what it will take to prepare a machine for processing a batch or multiple batches of material. A Setup can reference an external document and/or an InstructionSet to describe the setup work required.
Each Setup can also include a reference to a Recipe file for downloading to a machine. Recipe files are stored as Documents. The associated Document Viewer is the program to launch for downloading (the recipe) to a machine.; OriginalType: Setup

member.name: P:NCRCreateHistory.ChargeToStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 7199; FieldId: 10088; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: SpecStep

member.summary:
CdoId: 8000; FieldId: 17399; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:CollectDataHistory.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 8421; FieldId: 21600; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:CollectSamplingDataHistory.Product
member.summary:
CdoId: 8461; FieldId: 22090; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). member.name: P:MfgOperationHistory.Employee
member.summary:
CdoId: 8842; FieldId: 28207; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:MfgOperationHistory.MfgOrder
member.summary:
CdoId: 8842; FieldId: 26856; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.
; OriginalType: MfgOrder

member.name: P:MfgOperationHistory.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 8842; FieldId: 26857; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:MfgOperationHistory.WorkflowStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 8842; FieldId: 26858; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

member.name: P:ActivityStartHistory.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 9018; FieldId: 29305; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isMaterialRequestTxnHistory.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841589; FieldId: 702546999; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:isMaterialRequestTxnHistory.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841589; FieldId: 702547003; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isDefectHistory.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841553; FieldId: 702546741; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:IssueActualsHistory.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 6630; FieldId: 16913; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:SerializeHistoryDetails.ChildContainerLevel
member.summary:
CdoId: 6985; FieldId: 7695; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character. This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used. DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

member.name: P:EventLogHistoryDetail.Employee
member.summary:
CdoId: 8372; FieldId: 21392; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:SPCViolationHistoryDetail.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 8398; FieldId: 21219; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:SPCViolationHistoryDetail.ResourceStatusCode
member.summary:
CdoId: 8398; FieldId: 21430; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource Status Code is provides a description of the current availability for a Resource. This value is used for inquiry and in reporting. (Mean Time Between Failure, Mean Time to Repair, Time at Status, etc.).
Additionally, a Resource Status code identifies the default “Next” (Production) Transaction for a Resource. This is intended to be a simple implementation of a Resource Status Flow (Resource Workflow).; OriginalType: ResourceStatusCode

member.name: P:ActivityNextHistoryDetail.ActivityStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 9017; FieldId: 29291; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: SpecStep

member.name: P:ContainerMaintHistDetail.Level
member.summary:
CdoId: 7111; FieldId: 9323; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

member.name: P:ContainerMaintHistDetail.Location
member.summary: CdoId: 7111; FieldId: 9361; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Defines a physical location within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute. This is used to identify the physical location of the Container and produce reports such as WIP by Location.; OriginalType: Location

member.name: P:ContainerMaintHistDetail.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 7111; FieldId: 9363; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isDefectHistoryDetail.isOperation
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841552; FieldId: 702547607; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Operation is a manufacturing or processing point where inventory and production activities are tracked. The Operation describes such things as the reason codes, the work center, and the allowed transactions for the movement of material through a workflow step. In contrast, specifications define the specific processing that is performed at an operation.
The Operation also provides the general rules for the process and provides a general reporting construct. An Operation is referenced by a specification at a workflow step.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:isDefectHistoryDetail.isProduct
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841552; FieldId: 702546727; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:isDefectHistoryDetail.isRepairResource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841552; FieldId: 702547215; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isDefectHistoryDetail.isRepairSpec
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841552; FieldId: 702547231; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:isDefectHistoryDetail.isWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841552; FieldId: 702547217; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:isDefectHistoryDetail.isWorkflowStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841552; FieldId: 702547225; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: SpecStep

member.name: P:MaintenanceStatus.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 7347; FieldId: 11230; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:Step.ActivityPaths
member.summary:
CdoId: 1390; FieldId: 29270; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Path defines an allowable (Standard) move from one Step to another within a Workflow. Each Step contains zero or more (outbound) Paths. Only one of the Paths is the default Path, all others are alternate paths. If a Step contains any Paths, one must be the default. The default Route for a Workflow is determined by traversing through the Steps, starting at the first Step (defined in the workflow), using the default Path for each.
Paths are referenced by name or by Id. Path names are unique within the context of their Step.; OriginalType: MovePath

member.name: P:Step.ActivityPathSelectors
member.summary:
CdoId: 1390; FieldId: 29271; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Path selectors are used to select a Path based on the value of specific data within a transaction. Each Path selector includes an expression to evaluate and a Path to select. The expression must be a Boolean expression, and is defined using the standard InSite expression syntax.
A MovePathSelector is the path selector used for a normal path between steps, MovePathSelectors are evaluated by all Move-type transactions other than Rework and TransferRework. ReworkPathSelectors are evaluated by the Rework and TransferRework transactions. ; OriginalType: MovePathSelector

Each instance of a document (CDO) includes an identifier for the external document (i.e., a file name or a URL) and a reference to the program used for presenting the document.

member.name: P:BusinessRuleHandlerData.DisplayName
member.summary: CdoId: 7567; FieldId: 18158; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. The display name will include enough necessary elements to represent the object--in the example of a revisioned object it will include both the name and the revision, with a separator character. This is especially useful when viewing objects in combo boxes and other one-column lists, the display name should be used. DisplayName is usually a non-persistent field.

member.name: P:ProcessObject.Owner
member.summary:
CdoId: 7693; FieldId: 15321; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:ActivityStatus.ActivityState
member.summary: CdoId: 9016; FieldId: 29278; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Defines the current state for an activity step within a workflow:​ 0 - Not Set – the status has not been set.​ 1 - InQueue – the activity is InQueue.​ 2 - In Process – the activity has been started.​ 3 - Complete – the activity is complete​

member.name: P:ActivityStatus.ActivityStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 9016; FieldId: 29279; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: SpecStep

member.name: P:ActivityStatus.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 9016; FieldId: 29284; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. member.name: P:Activity.Owner
member.summary:
CdoId: 7694; FieldId: 15323; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:Phase.DisplayName
member.summary: CdoId: 7695; FieldId: 16365; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. CdoId: 7695; FieldId: 15324; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:ProductMaterialListItem.PhantomBill
member.summary: CdoId: 6080; FieldId: 15809; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A bill of material defines the materials needed to produce a specific product. A Phantom Bill is a bill of material for a product that does not exist as an actual assembly, but is created only for the purpose of holding a group of related components. A phantom bill is created to reduce maintenance efforts, when such a logical grouping of components is used for many finished products, so that the maintenance of the logical group of components can be done in one place only. member.summary: CdoId: 7930; FieldId: 16694; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A bill of material defines the materials needed to produce a specific product. A Phantom Bill is a bill of material for a product that does not exist as an actual assembly, but is created only for the purpose of holding a group of related components. A phantom bill is created to reduce maintenance efforts, when such a logical grouping of components is used for many finished products, so that the maintenance of the logical group of components can be done in one place only. member.summary: CdoId: 7033; FieldId: 8157; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A bill of material defines the materials needed to produce a specific product. A Phantom Bill is a bill of material for a product that does not exist as an actual assembly, but is created only for the purpose of holding a group of related components. A phantom bill is created to reduce maintenance efforts, when such a logical grouping of components is used for many finished products, so that the maintenance of the logical group of components can be done in one place only. Note the Phantom Bill referenced on the material list item directly will ordinarily just be a pointer to a bill defined as part of the associated Product referenced by the material list item. ; OriginalType: ERPBOM

member.name: P:SpecStep.Operation
member.summary:
CdoId: 1870; FieldId: 4506; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An instance of an Operation Definition describes an Operation to the application. Operations are logical (often times mapping to physical) descriptions of where work is to be performed. Operations also define rules for Shop Floor transactions. Another common use of Operations is to group WIP for reporting (i.e., WIP Status by Operation).
An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory. A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: Operation

member.name: P:SpecStep.PathSelectors
member.summary: CdoId: 1870; FieldId: 4834; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Paths selectors are used to select a Path based on the value(s) of specific data within a transaction. Each Path selector includes an expression to evaluate and a Path to select. The expression to evaluate identifies a field (see note 1) to evaluate and a comparison value. The comparison value can be a single value, a range (from-through values), or a list of values. Expressions are evaluated in a defined sequence. The first expression that evaluates to true determines the Path to select.

member.name: P:ContainerStatusDetails.ContainerLevel
member.summary:
CdoId: 6900; FieldId: 6803; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An instance of a Container describes a discrete unit of work (i.e., batch of material) including its current status within the manufacturing process, genealogy information and its relationship to other Containers. A Container typically represents a batch of material. It can also represent a group of batches of material. The grouping allow a single transaction to be applied to a related set of Containers. An example of this is tracking individual Packages and grouping them in a Carton. When the Carton is moved, all of the Packages within the Carton are moved as well.
Level codes are used to define a container level within a hierarchy. For example, a Lot may contain Wafers, which in turn contain Die. Each of these levels (Lot, Wafer, and Die) are have an associated Level Code. The attributes of the Level Code are used to define the relationship and other validations between levels. ; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

member.name: P:ContainerStatusDetails.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 6900; FieldId: 6781; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current status of each Preventative Maintenance for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Log-type Status Categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

CdoId: 7162; FieldId: 9856; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.summary: CdoId: 7162; FieldId: 9859; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource Status Reason Code is used to provide an added level of detail describing the reason for the current status of a Resource. For example, the current status may be REPAIR. A Status Reason Code can be used to provide additional details such as the type of repair that is being performed. This detail is included in the transaction history, which makes it available for Analysis Reporting.; OriginalType: ResourceStatusReason

The value is set (incremented) as part of the Resource Setup transaction. All Throughput and Movement transactions record this value in their history transactions.

member.name: P:ResourceStatusDetails.Setup
member.summary:
CdoId: 7162; FieldId: 9862; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Setup is a configuration of a resource needed to process a certain type of material (typcially a particular product, or a container referencing a particular spec).. Normally the definition of a setup includes only items as hardware configurations, that take significant time to change, while a reciipe would include many other items such as process settings that may be changed instantly.
Standard Camstar-provided attributes of a setup include items such as the applicable set of documents describing the setup configuration, an estimate of time need to configure the setup, etc. Setups are often defined in InSite to help provide scheduling/dispatching information on which containers/orders may be processed without significant changeover time between the items.
; OriginalType: Setup

member.name: P:GetMaintenanceStatusDetails.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 7359; FieldId: 11358; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

CdoId: 7656; FieldId: 15104; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee
