member.name: P:ApprovalCycleInquiryDetails.Approver
member.summary:
CdoId: 8004; FieldId: 17450; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:ChangePackageHeader.DocumentSets
member.summary: CdoId: 8486; FieldId: 24937; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Document Set is a list of one or more documents. Most Modeling entities include a reference to a Document Set. Documents are used in this context to provide extended (unstructured) information, such as product drawings, scanned images, relating existing manufacturing specifications, or operating procedures. Each instance of a Document (CDO) includes an identifier for the external document (i.e., a file name or a URL) and a reference to the program used for presenting the document.

member.name: P:ProcessTimerInquiryDetail.Product
member.summary:
CdoId: 8689; FieldId: 25235; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:ProcessTimerInquiryDetail.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 8689; FieldId: 25237; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

CdoId: 8926; FieldId: 27969; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.

CdoId: 4841525; FieldId: 702546416; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An instance of a Process Spec (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, InstructionSet, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:PartStatusDetails.Product
member.summary:
CdoId: 4751767; FieldId: 679481793; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:MatlContainerCurrentStartDtls.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 7944; FieldId: 16851; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.

member.name: P:ViewContainerAsParent.Container
member.summary: CdoId: 6901; FieldId: 23204; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).; OriginalType: Container

member.name: P:ViewContainerAsParent.ContainerLevel
member.summary:
CdoId: 6901; FieldId: 6816; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An instance of a Container describes a discrete unit of work (i.e., batch of material) including its current status within the manufacturing process, genealogy information and its relationship to other Containers. A Container typically represents a batch of material. It can also represent a group of batches of material. The grouping allow a single transaction to be applied to a related set of Containers. An example of this is tracking individual Packages and grouping them in a Carton. When the Carton is moved, all of the Packages within the Carton are moved as well.
Level codes are used to define a container level within a hierarchy. For example, a Lot may contain Wafers, which in turn contain Die. Each of these levels (Lot, Wafer, and Die) are have an associated Level Code. The attributes of the Level Code are used to define the relationship and other validations between levels. ; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

member.name: P:ViewContainerAsParent.DisplayName
member.summary: CdoId: 6901; FieldId: 9792; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: DisplayName is the field generally used to represent an object in a user interface, especially when the user interface needs to represent an object with just one data element. For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. member.name: P:ViewContainerAsParent.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 6901; FieldId: 6845; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current status of each Preventative Maintenance for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Log-type Status Categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:ContainerSearchDetail.ContainerLevel
member.summary:
CdoId: 8229; FieldId: 20150; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An instance of a Container describes a discrete unit of work (i.e., batch of material) including its current status within the manufacturing process, genealogy information and its relationship to other Containers. A Container typically represents a batch of material. It can also represent a group of batches of material. The grouping allow a single transaction to be applied to a related set of Containers. An example of this is tracking individual Packages and grouping them in a Carton. When the Carton is moved, all of the Packages within the Carton are moved as well.
Level codes are used to define a container level within a hierarchy. For example, a Lot may contain Wafers, which in turn contain Die. Each of these levels (Lot, Wafer, and Die) are have an associated Level Code. The attributes of the Level Code are used to define the relationship and other validations between levels. ; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

member.summary:
CdoId: 8229; FieldId: 20167; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current status of each Preventative Maintenance for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Log-type Status Categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. member.name: P:ContainerSearchDetail.Spec
member.summary:
CdoId: 8229; FieldId: 20171; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An instance of a Process Spec (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, InstructionSet, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:ContainerSearchDetail.Status
member.summary: CdoId: 8229; FieldId: 20174; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: Current status of this Container. This value is used to distinguish between Containers that are active, closed and those that have been deleted. Valid values and their meanings are: 0 = Deleted 1 = Active 2 = Closed 3 = In Transit (shipped) 4 = Issued (component) A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

member.name: P:ContainerSearchDetail.Step
member.summary:
CdoId: 8229; FieldId: 20175; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

member.name: P:ContainerSearchDetail.WorkCenter
member.summary:
CdoId: 8229; FieldId: 25866; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A work center is typically an area where work of a similar nature is performed. A work Center contains zero or more operations.
The work center is the component through which scheduling is performed through InSite. Scheduling can be conducted according to either employees or resources. A work center may have multiple operations if the operations are sharing employees, resources, or both. For example, an operation called Grind and an operation called Polish both use the same resources so they point to the same work center for scheduling purposes. There can also be one operation to one work center.
; OriginalType: WorkCenter

member.name: P:ContainerSearchDetail.Workflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 8229; FieldId: 20178; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:StartDetails.PrevWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 2370; FieldId: 28717; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:StartDetails.PriorityCode
member.summary: CdoId: 2370; FieldId: 1901; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An instance of a Priority Code is one method used to assign a processing priority to a Container. Each Priority Code includes a description and a Relative Priority value. The Relative Priority value is used to sequence Containers for dispatching (independent of the Code name or description). Priority Codes are only one of the algorithms used to determine a numeric value for Scheduling and Dispatching.; OriginalType: PriorityCode

member.name: P:StartDetails.Workstation
member.summary:
CdoId: 2370; FieldId: 25856; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:SerializeDetails.ChildContainerLevel
member.summary:
CdoId: 6988; FieldId: 7727; Workspace: csi; Flags: Required; Annotations: A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. member.name: P:SPCViolationDetail.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 8401; FieldId: 21241; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:SPCViolationDetail.ResourceStatusCode
member.summary:
CdoId: 8401; FieldId: 21419; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource Status Code is provides a description of the current availability for a Resource. This value is used for inquiry and in reporting. (Mean Time Between Failure, Mean Time to Repair, Time at Status, etc.).
Additionally, a Resource Status code identifies the default “Next” (Production) Transaction for a Resource. This is intended to be a simple implementation of a Resource Status Flow (Resource Workflow).; OriginalType: ResourceStatusCode

CdoId: 8504; FieldId: 22739; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

CdoId: 8577; FieldId: 702548262; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: Most Modeling entities include a reference to a document. Documents are used in this context to provide extended (unstructured) information, such as product drawings, scanned images, relating existing manufacturing specifications, or operating procedures. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. member.name: P:RPTProductWorkflowStepDetails.Product
member.summary:
CdoId: 8959; FieldId: 28480; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:RPTProductWorkflowStepDetails.RCount
member.summary: CdoId: 8959; FieldId: 28479; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: Record Count

member.name: P:RPTProductWorkflowStepDetails.Step
member.summary:
CdoId: 8959; FieldId: 28481; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A step is an individual tracking point within a workflow. The list of steps is the primary data structure within a workflow. Paths control the allowable movements between steps. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A Step normally represents an individual processing point in a workflow, where it references a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed. A Step can reference another workflow, in which case the step represents a series of processing points.; OriginalType: Step

member.name: P:RPTProductWorkflowStepDetails.Workflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 8959; FieldId: 28478; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:ContainerMaintDetail.Level
member.summary:
CdoId: 7109; FieldId: 9322; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

member.name: P:ContainerMaintDetail.Location
member.summary: CdoId: 7109; FieldId: 9360; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: Defines a physical location within a Factory. This can be as high level as a single Location that defines the entire Factory or as specific as individual Locations for each bin within a holding area. Every Container includes a Location attribute. This is used to identify the physical location of the Container and produce reports such as WIP by Location.; OriginalType: Location

member.name: P:ContainerMaintDetail.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 7109; FieldId: 9362; Workspace: csi; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:ContainerMaintDetail.SalesOrder

This equates to a line item on a typical (ERP) Sales Order. Containers are optionally assigned to a Sales Order (by specifying the Sales Order as an attribute). This provides the mechanism for relating WIP (Containers) to Customer Orders.; OriginalType: SalesOrder

member.name: P:isDefectDetail.isRepairResource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841548; FieldId: 702547227; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isDefectDetail.isRepairSpec
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841548; FieldId: 702547229; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.summary:
CdoId: 4841548; FieldId: 702547223; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:isDefectDetail.isWorkflowStep
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841548; FieldId: 702548200; Workspace: 15; Flags: None; Annotations: Steps are used to discretely define processing for a point (step) within a Workflow. A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are related using Paths. Each Step contains zero or more Paths, which link to another Step. One Path at each Step is identified as the default Path.
A sequence of Steps and Paths is a Route. A Workflow can include multiple Routes. Only one Route is identified as the Standard Route. The Standard Route is determined by starting with the Step that is identified as the first Step and then iterating forward selecting the default path at each step.
A Specification Step is a step within a Workflow that includes a reference to a Spec which in turn describes the work that is to be performed.
; OriginalType: SpecStep

member.summary:
CdoId: 1580; FieldId: 702548206; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. member.name: P:MasterRecipe.Workflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 7933; FieldId: 16788; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:ERPBOM.ERPRoute
member.summary: CdoId: 7026; FieldId: 8377; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: ERP Routes are the closest ERP concept to an InSite workflow. The ERPRoute object in InSite is meant to be a mirror of the route definitions in the ERP, where the definition stored in the ERP is the "master" and the InSite ERPRoute is populated via LiveConnect. The ERPRoute is used to be able to relate InSite Moves and ComponentIssues to the ERPStep where the transaction occurred. Steps in an ERP route are usually defined at a more summarized level than is true for steps in an InSite workflow.; OriginalType: ERPRoute

member.name: P:Spec.MaxQueueTime
member.summary:
CdoId: 1820; FieldId: 338; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: This is not implemented in the current version of InSite.
This value determines the maximum length of time a Container can remain in an in-queue state at the Step that uses this Spec. The value for MaximumQueueTimeAction determines the action to take if the in-queue time exceeds this value.

member.name: P:Spec.MaxQueueTimeAction
member.summary:
CdoId: 1820; FieldId: 339; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: This is not implemented in the current version of InSite.
This value is used to determine the action to take when a Service (transaction) is started for a Container that has been in-queue longer than the allowable queue time (MaxQueueTime).
The values for this option are: 0 = No action 1 = Warning to Operator 2 = Warning to Operator requiring a password to continue 3 = Place container on Hold 4 = Do not allow transaction to continue
These values and their associated actions are intended to match the values and actions for field validations.
This action applies to any service that changes a Container from an In-Queue to an In-Process state.

member.name: P:Employee.EscalationRecipients
member.summary:
CdoId: 1140; FieldId: 24968; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:Factory.FHMResolvedAllResources
member.summary:
CdoId: 1250; FieldId: 27123; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Used for the "Factory Hiararchy Model". Get all resources for a factory with a factory level set. This provides a 'flat' version of the resource hiararchy.
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

member.name: P:Factory.FHMResolvedAreaResources
member.summary:
CdoId: 1250; FieldId: 27124; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Used for the "Factory Hiararchy Model". Get all resources for a factory with a factory level set to "Area". The tree of child resources can then be traversed.
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:Factory.isCarrierWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 1250; FieldId: 702547326; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. member.name: P:Resource.FHMResolvedChildResources
member.summary:
CdoId: 1490; FieldId: 27125; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Used with the factory hiararchy model. Get all children of this resource with a factory level set.
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:MfgOrder.isResolvedWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 1620; FieldId: 702547638; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:ShipmentDestination.LocalContainerStatus
member.summary: CdoId: 6974; FieldId: 7894; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Status of the Container on the Local Site that is being set when it is sent to the ShipmentDestination. Current status of this Container. This value is used to distinguish between Containers that are active, closed and those that have been deleted. Valid values and their meanings are: 0 = Deleted 1 = Active 2 = Closed 3 = In Transit (shipped) 4 = Issued (component) A deleted Container is one where all of the transactions, including the Create (or Split-to) transaction have been reversed.

member.name: P:ShipmentDestination.Location
member.summary: CdoId: 6974; FieldId: 7588; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Defines a physical location within a Factory. member.name: P:DataTransport.DisplayName

For example, to represent a revisioned object one would ordinarily need to show both the name and the revision of the object. member.name: P:MaintenanceClass.Resources
member.summary:
CdoId: 7338; FieldId: 11195; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:EMailDistribution.EmployeeRecipients
member.summary:
CdoId: 7549; FieldId: 13131; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

CdoId: 8869; FieldId: 27169; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

member.name: P:ShopFloorSettings.Workflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 8869; FieldId: 27167; Workspace: csi; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:CIOCamstarConnection.UserName
member.summary:
CdoId: 4726787; FieldId: 673185860; Workspace: 10; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: An Employee is a person that can login to InSite, perform transactions, and/or be credited with work. The Employees must have a Windows NT account. Once defined, the user will then appear in the user list within the Modeler Security window. In this way the Employee definition feeds directly into the Modeler Security.
The Employee definitions also allow for other options for each user such as the factory associate with the user and the language that will be used. Persons that will get credited with work by being entered in the employee field on a transaction, must exist as InSite employees, but are not required to exist as Windows user accounts.; OriginalType: Employee

member.name: P:CIOChannelAdapter.CIOMessageChannel
member.summary: CdoId: 4726788; FieldId: 673185888; Workspace: 10; Flags: Required, ReadOnly; Annotations: A logical address for the CIO Messaging System. Messages pass through a Message Channel as they flow to or from the Message Broker. Channel Messages are converted to and from an internal Message format. This internal format carries metadata and message contents in Xml format with UTF-8 encoding. The Message Channel provides filter pipelines where both standard and custom filter plugins are processed against a message to alter its contents - including conversions to and from UTF-8. This provides an extensibility point to handle very specific customizations.; OriginalType: CIOMessageChannel

member.name: P:CIOChannelSource.CIOMessageChannel
member.summary: CdoId: 4726789; FieldId: 673185910; Workspace: 10; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A logical address for the CIO Messaging System. Messages pass through a Message Channel as they flow to or from the Message Broker. Channel Messages are converted to and from an internal Message format. This internal format carries metadata and message contents in Xml format with UTF-8 encoding. The Message Channel provides filter pipelines where both standard and custom filter plugins are processed against a message to alter its contents - including conversions to and from UTF-8. This provides an extensibility point to handle very specific customizations.; OriginalType: CIOMessageChannel

member.name: P:CIOMessageType.EventOnly
member.summary:
CdoId: 4726794; FieldId: 673187841; Workspace: 10; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Channel Adapters can be configured for both inbound and outbound DoNotSend mode. In this mode, messages are buffered but the buffers are in offline mode. In this mode all calls to Peek or Get are ignored (thus not sending them on to their destination). In this mode, calls to Get Newest are processed and the newest message in the offline buffer is returned (also purging any older messages). The Get Newest is used to support the Get Message Web API call that is used by the Map Client.
This functionality is provided to allow specific messages to not be buffered nor sent to the Broker but to be available for SignalR Eventing (by subscribed clients).
This feature will add the ability to designate a specific message type as being EventOnly even when processed by an Adapter that is not in this mode.

member.name: P:isPreactorSchedule.isWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841482; FieldId: 702547185; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:isInventoryLocation.isParentResource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841507; FieldId: 702547779; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isMaterialRequestStatus.Resource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841585; FieldId: 702546965; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:isAutoStartSettings.isLevel
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841582; FieldId: 702546935; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Container Level is the tracking designation assigned to a container. The level identifies the position of the container within a container structure. A container is defined within InSite as a discrete collection of products produced in a factory.
Each container has a unique identifier used for traceability and performance of shop floor transactions. Commonly used level names are batch and lot. Container Levels are defined to meet the specific requirements of each company. Examples of some industry-specific levels are roll, bin, and cassette. Many companies also track smaller levels within the larger, parent container. With InSite, this is accomplished through multi-level tracking. Parent and child level containers are associated using the Associate, Combine or Group Start transactions. For example, a group of containers can have a parent with a batch level and associated child containers with tray levels. Container groups can also have more than two levels.; OriginalType: ContainerLevel

member.name: P:isAutoStartSettings.isOwner
member.summary: CdoId: 4841582; FieldId: 702546936; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Every Container has an associated Owner Code. The owner code is used as a grouping to separate Containers for inquiry and processing. Examples of Owner Code are "Manufacturing", "Engineering", "Prototypes", "SalesSamples", etc.; OriginalType: Owner

member.summary: CdoId: 4841582; FieldId: 702547589; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Product Type Codes are used to differentiate between types of product such as WIP, Raw Material, Finished Goods, etc.; OriginalType: ProductType

member.name: P:isAutoStartSettings.isStartReason
member.summary: CdoId: 4841582; FieldId: 702546932; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Each Container has an associated Start Code. Start Codes are available for selection criteria on WIP Status Inquiries and for transaction reporting (based on the transaction history).; OriginalType: StartReason

member.name: P:isAutoStartSettings.isWorkflow
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841582; FieldId: 702546938; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Workflow defines the route and processing required for a manufacturing process, and is the primary driving object of the InSite factory model. When a Container is created (started) it references a Workflow (and a Step within that Workflow). The default Workflow for the Start transaction is the Workflow referenced in the Product definition.
A Workflow is a collection of Steps that are linked by Paths and ReworkPaths. Steps reference either other Workflows or Specs, and a Spec references an Operation. Note that the definition of Step, Spec, and Operation controls the processing details at any individual point in the workflow.; OriginalType: Workflow

member.name: P:CIOWebAPIClientAdapter.CIOProcessResponse
member.summary:
CdoId: 4727028; FieldId: 673188003; Workspace: 10; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: ProcessResponse: String enumeration indicating how to process a response.
Valid values are:
None: do not generate a response message. Non-Ok status will cause a retry.
Content: return a response message from the contents of the response if the status is ok. Non-Ok status will cause a retry.
Status: return a response message that contains the status code and reason phrase. Non-Ok status will cause a message to be generated not a retry.
ContentsOrStatus: return a response message that contains either the contents. Empty contents or a non-Ok status code will return a response message containing the status code and reason phrase. Non-Ok status will not cause a retry.

member.name: P:CarrierFamily.isMfgOrder
member.summary:
CdoId: 7903; FieldId: 702547789; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.
; OriginalType: MfgOrder

member.name: P:CarrierFamily.isProduct
member.summary:
CdoId: 7903; FieldId: 702547791; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:Carrier.isMfgOrder
member.summary:
CdoId: 7902; FieldId: 702547781; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Manufacturing Order is a request to manufacture a product. Manufacturing orders are typically originated to fulfill a sales order or inventory requirements and are often a link between MES and an ERP system.
A Manufacturing Order can contain a list of product containers. The relationship of a container to a manufacturing order is established and maintained in the containers data record. This information is used to provide WIP status by manufacturing order and WIP updates to the ERP system.
; OriginalType: MfgOrder

member.name: P:Carrier.isProduct
member.summary:
CdoId: 7902; FieldId: 702547783; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Product is typically a definition of what kind of material needs to be provided to a customer or what kind of material is being used as a raw material or other component in a manufacturing process. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.
Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.; OriginalType: Product

member.name: P:Carrier.isResource
member.summary:
CdoId: 7902; FieldId: 702547369; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.
A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.; OriginalType: Resource

member.name: P:Carrier.isSingleProduct

member.name: P:Carrier.isSpec
member.summary:
CdoId: 7902; FieldId: 702547370; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.
A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.
See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.; OriginalType: Spec

member.name: P:Carrier.isTrackingContainer
member.summary: CdoId: 7902; FieldId: 702547367; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: A Container describes a discrete unit of work or a discrete quantity of material (i.e., batch of material, a serialized component or serialized piece of material, a uniquely identified package or vessel that contains product, etc.) A Container can include quantity information (weight, count, etc.) directly, or it can include a grouping of other containers (child containers).; OriginalType: Container

member.name: P:isDevice.CIOChannelAdapter
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841472; FieldId: 702546045; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Channel Adapters provide an abstraction between the source system and the CIO Messaging System to allow the source system to send messages to the CIO Messaging System and receive messages from the CIO Messaging System without requiring the source system to directly consume the CIO endpoints. Channel Adapters provide a layer of abstraction to the external application to 'adapt' the Message Channel for convenience. Examples of Channel Adapters can be as simple as providing shared directories for passing files back and forth or as complex as accessing a source application's API to invoke the functionality inside an application necessary to retrieve and send data.
Camstar provides a standard set of Channel Adapters (e.g. ByFileAdapter), however, custom adapters can also be created for specific purposes (reference the Camstar CIO SDK).
; OriginalType: CIOChannelAdapter

member.name: P:isDevice.CIOChannelSource
member.summary:
CdoId: 4841472; FieldId: 702546041; Workspace: 15; Flags: ReadOnly; Annotations: Channel Source
Messages can be sent to the CIO Messaging System directly, without use of a Channel Adapter. In this case, the Source system must interact directly with the exposed CIO Endpoints. The CIO Messaging System exposes a one-way service endpoint for messages inbound to the system and consumes a one-way service endpoint for messages being sent outbound.
; OriginalType: CIOChannelSource
